Subject: PHI handling and BAA — quick clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. We're doing the final security review ahead of procurement. Attached is our short HIPAA questionnaire — a few points came up that need a plain-language confirmation from engineering/legal before we proceed to contract:

- Will Redwood act as a Business Associate for services that process PHI if we sign a BAA?
- For hosted API usage: does Redwood persist transcript/output beyond the immediate inference call? If so, where/how long?
- Can we use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest in Hosted or only in Dedicated/Private deployments?
- Are there configuration options to ensure no PHI is written to long-term storage (audit logs excluded)?
- Do you offer a signed attestation that PHI is isolated from other tenants (logical isolation, no shared buckets with PHI)?

We're not asking for full SOC 2 artifacts yet — just targeted clarifications to feed to our legal and privacy teams.

Attached: CareBridge_HIPAA_Questionnaire.xlsx

Appreciate a short, bulletized reply we can share with procurement.

Best,
Jenna Park

Hi Jenna (and team),

Below are concise, engineering-backed answers you can share with procurement/legal. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through any of the items.

1) BAA: Yes — Redwood will sign a standard BAA to cover our hosted API, Dedicated, and Private offerings. When signed, Redwood will be treated as a Business Associate for covered processing activities described in the BAA. The draft attached is the version we typically start with.

2) Persistence of transcript/output: By default, for hosted API customers Redwood does NOT write model-generated outputs or customer prompts to durable long-term user-facing storage. Processing flow: incoming request -> in-memory batching & KV cache for attention/context -> inference -> streamed response. Short-lived artifacts (KV cache entries) are kept only for the duration required to serve the request and for the configured cache TTL (default 120s) to support low-latency re-requests. Customers can opt-in to explicit persistence features (e.g., logging or dataset export) — these are off by default.

3) Customer-managed keys: Customer-managed encryption keys are supported in Redwood Private and Dedicated (with KMS/HSM integrations). For Hosted API we offer encryption in transit and at rest with Redwood-managed keys; enterprise customers on Dedicated can bring keys via AWS KMS/GCP KMS integrations or on-prem HSM. If you require customer-key-only storage for any PHI artifacts, Dedicated/Private is the recommended model.

4) No long-term storage option: Yes — we can configure your tenant such that no PHI is written to durable object storage. That configuration turns off optional persistence features and removes dataset exports from the UI for your account. Note: system-level audit logs (access timestamps, API call metadata) are retained for security and troubleshooting; we can discuss retention windows.

5) Tenant isolation attestation: Redwood uses strict logical isolation for customer data. Hosted API requests are routed to multi-tenant inference pools; PHI is isolated in per-tenant namespaces, and buckets that may contain customer artifacts are logically separated. For customers requiring stronger guarantees (physical isolation, dedicated VMs/GPU pools, customer-managed KMS), Dedicated or Private deployments provide dedicated capacity and network isolation. We can supply an attestation statement and reference to our SOC 2 controls describing logical isolation.

Additional notes:
- Auditability: We expose detailed per-request logs and a tenant-level audit trail for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted API we can provide a targeted log export for compliance review.
- DPIA / regulatory support: Our privacy team can pull together a DPIA summary describing data flows for your legal/privacy reviewers.
- Timeline: If you want the signed BAA + configuration that disables persistence, we can get a legal-approved DocuSign within 3–5 business days once commercial terms are agreed.

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Draft_2026-07-28.pdf, redwood-privacy-datasheet.pdf

Regards,
